newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh former president Ershad ill.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh former president Ershad ill.

text.p: Former Bangladesh president Hossain Mohammad Ershad is suffering from chest pains and has cancelled a four-day tour of northern districts, his brother said on Saturday.
G.M. Quader told reporters that the Jatiya Party chief had fallen sick on Friday night and was being flown to Dhaka for treatment.
Doctors in Rangpur, his northern home town, advised Ershad, 68, to take complete rest. The cause of the chest pains was not immediately clear.
Ershad, a retired general, seized power in a 1982 bloodless coup but was deposed in a popular uprising in December 1990.
In 1991 he was jailed for 13 years on charges of corruption and illegal possession of arms while in power, and served more than five years before his release on bail in January.
He had meanwhile been elected to parliament in the June 1996 general election which he contested from his jail cell.
Last week Ershad hit the headlines with reports that his wife had briefly left him in a row over his alleged relationship with Zinat Mosharraf, a Jatiya Party woman legislator.
Newspapers said his wife, Begum Roushan, had gone to live with her sister but Ershad had persuaded her to return home.
They quoted the president, however, as denying there had been any family crisis. His wife was unavailable for comment.
